content:
Joel - first you need to provide more details. Are you on a Mac or a PC? What operating system version are you using? Where are you getting your email? Is it a private Host, like QTH.com, or one of the common sources like gmail.com or Yahoo.com?

All those details point to different situations.

In my case, the standard TB configuration provided a Spam folder that at one time was called "Junk". When I right-clicked it, viewed its properties, and checked the path, it ended with "/Junk".

But my email host's software also added their own spam folder. Its path ended in "/spam".

I kept trying to unsubscribe from THAT spam folder (unsubscribe is a right-click on the Home account), but because it was created by my email host, it kept reappearing. Then I realized I should be unsubscribing from the spam folder that came with the TB setup. When I unchecked that (unsubscribed), that folder went away, so I then only had one - the one my Host creates. I checked Spam Management and made sure the checkboxes routed any spam email to the remaining spam folder under the Home account.

So my solution depended on the situation that I was working on a Windows 11 Pro PC and Laptop. And that I had an emial host for my quickdata account. And that the host's software (Spam Assassin) would identify potential spam, but - as agreed by me - would send it to me anyway, identified as spam, because sometimes legitimate email gets mistakenly labeled spam.

Your mileage may vary. Good Luck.

I am not a Windows person; I just have them for occasional compatibility issues. And I'm not a network person. I just saw that though both folders were named "Spam", they had different paths. And I'm used TB long enough that I remembered the Junk Folder. And googling gave me a hint that the second spam folder was being created by my email host. I spent an hour or so trying to delete that one (the unsubscribe action), before I realized I should be unsubscribing form the "/Junk" path spam folder and keeping the other.
